AMZN.rationale: Amazon demonstrates strong fundamental health with accelerating revenue growth (Q3 2025: +13.4% YoY, +7.4% QoQ) and robust earnings expansion (EPS +36.4% YoY). The company maintains a dominant competitive position with 40.5% U.S. e-commerce market share and 32% global cloud infrastructure share through AWS. Operating margins have improved to 11% with net margins at 11.1%, while the balance sheet remains strong with $369.6B equity against only $55.1B debt. However, the massive $200B capex commitment for 2026 creates near-term free cash flow compression risk, and the stock trades at a P/E of 36.2x—near the upper end of its 365-day range (28.2-40.9x). The upcoming Q1 2026 earnings report on April 29 represents a potential catalyst, with analysts expecting $1.69 EPS and AWS growth acceleration to 28%. News sentiment is moderately positive (mean 0.298 over 90 days), and the Globalstar acquisition strengthens the satellite internet competitive position against SpaceX. The valuation is fair-to-slightly-rich versus recent history, limiting upside from current levels despite strong fundamentals.

sources_cited.excerpt: Amazon claimed the top spot among online retailers in the United States in 2025, capturing 40.5 percent of the market
Amazon's AWS maintained its position as the global leader in cloud infrastructure services, holding approximately 32% of the total public cloud IaaS and PaaS market
Amazon committed approximately $200 billion in capital expenditure for full-year 2026, a 53% increase from the $131.8 billion deployed in 2025
Amazon announced an $11.6 billion acquisition of satellite service provider Globalstar to advance its Leo satellite internet project
Amazon stock has rallied nearly 30% in recent weeks to around $250, driven by improved confidence in its AI investments

Amazon.com is set to announce its first-quarter results next week, with analysts projecting single-digit growth in its bottom-line figure. EPS of $1.69, up 6.3% from $1.59 per share in the same quarter last year
